text: The Monitor hub from Lesson 38 is something you check. Alerts are the opposite: Data Factory tells you, the moment a condition you defined is actually met — no need to be staring at the runs list when a production pipeline fails at three in the morning.

From Monitor, Alerts and metrics, New alert rule opens the entry point for every alert you'll create in this data factory. The metric list covers nearly every failure category you'd genuinely want to know about — not just a generic something broke, but failed activity runs, failed pipeline runs, failed trigger runs, cancelled runs of each, and integration runtime health metrics like CPU utilization and available memory.

A raw any-activity-anywhere-failed alert gets noisy fast, and noisy alerts genuinely get ignored. Scope it down by dimension: filter by ActivityType, ActivityName, or PipelineName, so a truly critical nightly load pipeline can have its own dedicated, tightly-scoped alert, separate from everything else running in the factory.

Every execution activity carries a policy block: timeout, retry, retryIntervalInSeconds, and secureOutput. The default is genuinely zero retries — you have to opt in. For a Copy activity pulling from a flaky REST API, setting retry to three with a thirty to sixty second interval quietly absorbs transient failures that would otherwise page someone for absolutely nothing.

Alerts and retries solve two real, different problems: retries try to prevent a transient failure from becoming your problem at all, while alerts make sure that when something genuinely does fail, you find out immediately instead of stumbling onto it later. Next: Error Handling Patterns — designing pipelines that fail gracefully, not just pipelines that fail.
